correctness.rationale: Order adherence A(S) is monotone and positively homogeneous for full order-convergent nets. From r-demicontinuity, A(B_F) subset r B_F; induction gives A^n(B_F) subset r^n B_F for every finite n, including n=0. For r>1, norm>x>1 requires n>=ceil(log_r ||x||); the bound cannot cover unbounded nonzero F at any finite n. Anti-semicontinuity says order closure of B_F is F and closure is formed by transfinite adherence, so such coexistence would require at least a limit stage omega. For nonzero order-continuous bounded functional phi, the proper strip {|phi(x)|<=||phi||} is order-closed and contains B_F; its properness contradicts anti-semicontinuity. This independently establishes F_oc*=0 as a necessary condition. No claim of existence or impossibility is proved.

The claim neither says the coexistence problem is solved nor sells the induction as a major theorem; the finite-depth barrier has precise use when eliminating candidate examples.
